column1: # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
# Proof debt for the Creusot amendment, issue #121.
# Every place the kernel steps outside the proof gets a row here, naming the
# tool limitation that forced it.  A row is an admission, not an excuse: the
# question each one answers is "what would a prover have caught here, and what
# is catching it instead?"
# The ledger is enforced by scripts/creusot_ledger_check.sh, which enumerates
# the escapes on disk and compares them against these rows in BOTH directions.
# An unledgered escape is red; a row naming an escape that no longer exists is
# red too, so the ledger cannot grow silently and cannot rot quietly either.
# Mechanisms:
#   trusted      an empty contract via #[cfg_attr(creusot, ..::trusted)].
#                Assumes nothing about the body, so it stays sound, but the
#                body is unverified.
#   cfg-out      an item compiled out under cfg(creusot), placing it outside
#                the proof boundary.  Two forms: a derive dropped from a
#                cfg_attr(not(creusot), derive(..)) list, or a whole
#                hand-written #[cfg(not(creusot))] impl Trait for Type.
#                Keyed by DERIVE-OR-TRAIT NAME, one row per name, because the
#                escape is a property of the trait and not of the type it sits
#                on -- so swapping a derive for an equivalent hand-written
#                impl keeps the row it already had instead of quietly changing
#                shape and walking out of the gate's view.
#   no-contract  a function with no functional postcondition.  Creusot still
#                discharges it for panic- and overflow-freedom; what is absent
#                is a statement of what it computes.
# Columns: id  path  item  mechanism  reason  evidence  retire_when
PD-01
column5: Returns f32. Creusot 0.13 implements DeepModel for char, str, String, bool, Int, Ordering, (), the integer types, Duration, Instant, BigRational, PeanoInt and Id -- and no float type, so there is no logical model of IEEE-754 to state a postcondition in.
column6: creusot-std-0.13.0/src/std/cmp.rs:26 specs partial_cmp via deep_model() unconditionally; a DeepModel impl for f64/f32 is absent from the crate.
column7: Creusot ships a float theory, or fraction() is moved behind an integer-valued API (it is display-only; nothing in the determinism kernel reads it).

column1: PD-02
column5: Returns f64 (u32 / 2^32). Same absent float model as PD-01. The contract is empty, so it assumes nothing; the integer step it wraps, next_u32, IS proved.
column6: Same as PD-01. Byte-exactness of the division is guarded by the golden replay tests and the libm pin (ADR-0004), not by Creusot.

column1: PD-03
column5: A derived Serialize translates but does not prove. Serialization is outside the proof boundary either way: the determinism claim is about the values, not their wire form.
column6: Goal Coma.vc_serialize_Cfg: FAIL (24/28), measured on an isolation crate.
column7: serde derives carry contracts, or the impl is hand-written with one. Neither is worth it for a boundary the kernel does not depend on.

column1: PD-04
column5: Paired with PD-03; the same derive family and the same boundary. Kept as its own row because the gate keys on derive names, so a row per name is what makes the bijection exact.

column1: PD-05
column5: Hand-written and compiled out entirely under cfg(creusot).  It does not prove: Hasher is an external trait with no contract, and Creusot warns that calling a contractless external function "will yield an impossible precondition", so a green result here would be vacuous rather than meaningful.  Hashing is not part of any determinism invariant either -- Alert is compared by value, and its PartialEq IS hand-written and proved.  Hand-written rather than derived because clippy::derived_hash_with_manual_eq rejects a derived Hash beside a hand-written eq; it hashes the discriminant, so it agrees with that eq by construction.
column6: Goal Coma.vc_hash_Alert: FAIL, measured on the derived form before the swap.

column1: PD-06
column5: A PRNG step has no useful functional postcondition -- being hard to characterise is its purpose. The proof is NOT vacuous: every operation is wrapping or masking, and discharging the function proves it panic- and overflow-free for all 2^32 states.
column6: An earlier draft specced result@ == state@ + 1, which is FALSE at u32::MAX -- a false contract is a mutant that passes for the wrong reason. Recorded so it is not reintroduced. The bit-exact output vector is pinned by the unit test seed_123456_u32_vector.
column7: Never, deliberately. This row exists to make the absence a decision on the record rather than an oversight.
